extracted.intended_audience: readers and practitioners interested in colonial exploration, coastal surveying, and settlement (explorers, surveyors, colonial administrators, settlers)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria implicit in a 19th-century exploration/survey travelogue for judging harbours, land suitability, and map accuracy. Covers how to observe anchors/shore features, assess soil/vegetation/water, and verify chart positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for settlement (three necessary articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: "this part of the country was not fit for the settler, being deficient in the three most necessary articles, water, timber for building, and food for stock.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct on-the-ground observation to check for reliable fresh water sources, sufficient timber of usable size, and pasture or food resources for livestock; absence of these is a clear negative for settlement. Examples in text: arid plains, brackish pools, and only small stunted trees render country unsuitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harbour / anchorage quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess anchorage by shelter from prevailing winds, depth (fathoms), holding ground, entrance hazards (reefs, sandbanks), and exposure in gales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a bay provides shelter from northerly/westerly/seaward winds; note soundings (e.g., 7–60 fathoms), presence of reefs or sandbanks that let sea enter in gales, and holding ground (e.g., 'mud with a coating of sand' praised). A harbour exposed to winter gales (e.g., wreck in head of Koombanah Bay) is unsafe without artificial works like breakwaters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chart and position verification (surveying accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct charts and positions by meridian distances, bearings to conspicuous peaks, chronometer error checks, triangulation, and magnetical observations (note map latitudinal/longitudinal errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take bearings of landmarks (Mount William, Cape Naturaliste, etc.), determine latitudes/longitudes, compare to existing charts (Arrowsmith, Captain King's chart), and record discrepancies (several places laid down miles too far north). Use chronometer checks and triangulation where possible to refine positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soil and fertility indicators (vegetation and deposits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Soil quality inferred from vegetation types (stunted vs tall trees), presence of alluvial deposits, limestone outcrops, ironstone/quartz fragments, and native-root digging evidence (warran).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe whether plains are sandy scrub or have light mould near watercourses; look for alluvial beds near cliffs or watercourses indicating richer soil; deeper holes dug by natives and abundance of warran may point to local fertility, but widespread sandy subsoil indicates sterility. Use detailed ground inspection rather than distant eye-judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fresh-water source identification and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between salt estuaries, brackish pools, dry stream beds, and native wells; test water salinity and probe for deeper sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace estuaries inland to determine whether water is fresh or salt (text: mouth of Greenough entirely salt). When streams are dry, dig in beds and hollows; native wells (found under drooping gums) can be discovered and deepened to yield water. Note bank composition and depth to sand/alluvium for water potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timber and building-material availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge availability by tree size and species (large straight gums vs stunted scrub) and presence of suitable timber on ridges and in valleys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small stunted banksia, wattles and drooping gums are insufficient for building materials; isolated clumps in dried watercourses may be better but overall scarcity of large timber is a negative for settlement and construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food for stock and game abundance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess quantity of feed and wild animals (kangaroos, emus, wallaby) as indicators of capacity to support stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sparse sightings (e.g., only three kangaroos and five emus observed) and prevalence of coarse brown grass/prickly bush indicate poor grazing; presence of only small patches of useful grass (three or four acres) is not adequate for large-scale pastoral use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnetic anomaly and compass reliability near ironstone
rubrics_metrics.description: Large ironstone formations can deflect the magnetic needle by significant degrees (text: 'changing its direction in different places ten degrees').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that local ironstone masses or mineral deposits will corrupt compasses; take magnetical observations and cross-check bearings with other methods (celestial observation) to avoid position errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estuary/river mouth navigability and entrance hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether an estuary is connected to the sea by a visible entrance, whether sandhills overlap to hide the mouth, bank heights, and the tendency of the sea to enter in gales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace estuary mouths on foot/boat; note if a low sand bank separates it from the sea and whether the entrance is discoverable from seaward. High banks of limestone or sand can hide or alter entrances, and gales may force sea over low banks—hazard for navigation and anchorage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use caution when inferring land quality from distant/vague observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Eyeball judgments from a distance (as by Moore) can be too vague to ascertain tree types, grassiness, or water sufficiency; ground inspection is required for reliable conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on distant views to declare a district fertile; corroborate with ground-based soil/vegetation/water inspections. The text contrasts Moore's distant hopeful account ('may turn out to be the finest') with on-the-ground findings of sterility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of transport infrastructure feasibility (road → railroad)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate existing roads for width, level, and potential conversion to railway, and consider port draught limitations affecting cargo handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect road width (sufficient for single rail line without detracting value), level of terrain (a complete level is advantageous), and port limitations (Port of Adelaide admits only moderate-draught vessels—large ships must transship at Holdfast Roads), to judge commercial viability of a railroad linking port and town.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in land allocation / treatment of squatters (policy criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of Special Survey system and principle that squatters who developed land deserve purchase rights or compensation for improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy-wise, favor mechanisms allowing squatters to purchase land they occupy by private contract or receive allowances equivalent to improvements; watch for special-survey purchases that displace smallholders by speculative buyers.
